claim: Phase transitions of linear multivalent proteins control the reversible formation of many intracellular membraneless bodies.
source: Phase transitions of linear multivalent proteins control the reversible formation of many intracellular membraneless bodies.
evidence: This is a general statement in the abstract that is supported by the broader literature context and the study's focus.

claim: Gelation transitions can occur with or without phase separation.
source: Gelation transitions can occur with or without phase separation.
evidence: This is a central premise of the study, supported by theoretical frameworks and the simulations presented.

claim: Gelation driven by phase separation requires lower protein concentrations than gelation without phase separation.
source: Gelation driven by phase separation requires lower protein concentrations, and seems to be the biologically preferred mechanism for forming membraneless bodies.
evidence: This claim is supported by the simulation results showing lower concentration thresholds for phase separation-driven gelation.

claim: Gelation driven by phase separation is the biologically preferred mechanism for forming membraneless bodies.
source: Gelation driven by phase separation requires lower protein concentrations, and seems to be the biologically preferred mechanism for forming membraneless bodies.
evidence: This is presented as a speculation based on the lower concentration requirements and biological observations.

claim: Intrinsically disordered linkers determine the extent to which gelation of linear multivalent proteins is driven by phase separation.
source: Here, we use coarse-grained computer simulations and the theory of associative polymers to uncover the physical properties of intrinsically disordered linkers that determine the extent to which gelation of linear multivalent proteins is driven by phase separation.
evidence: This is the main finding of the study, supported by computational simulations and theoretical analysis.

claim: Biomolecular condensates are two- or three-dimensional assemblies that comprise of multiple proteins and RNA molecules and lack a surrounding membrane.
source: These are two- or three-dimensional assemblies that comprise of multiple proteins and RNA molecules and lack a surrounding membrane.
evidence: This is a definitional statement based on established knowledge in the field.

claim: Biomolecular condensates are associated with a range of cellular functions including cell signaling, ribosomal biogenesis, cytoskeletal regulation, stress response, cell polarization, and cytoplasmic branching.
source: Biomolecular condensates are associated with a range of cellular functions including cell signaling (Su et al., 2016), ribosomal biogenesis (Feric et al., 2016; Zhu and Brangwynne, 2015; Mitrea et al., 2016), cytoskeletal regulation (Li et al., 2012; Banjade and Rosen, 2014), stress response (Parry et al., 2014; Munder et al., 2016; Ramaswami et al., 2013; Riback et al., 2017), cell polarization (Saha et al., 2016; Nott et al., 2015), and cytoplasmic branching (Lee et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Scaffold proteins drive phase transitions, whereas client molecules preferentially partition from the cytoplasm or nucleoplasm into condensates.
source: Scaffolds are thought to drive phase transitions, whereas client molecules preferentially partition from the cytoplasm or nucleoplasm into condensates (Banani et al., 2016; Wheeler et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a conceptual framework supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Scaffold proteins that drive phase transitions have multivalency of folded domains or Short Linear amino acid Motifs (SLiMs) as a prominent feature.
source: Scaffold proteins that drive phase transitions have distinct features, the most prominent being multivalency of folded domains or Short Linear amino acid Motifs (SLiMs) (Banani et al., 2017; Li et al., 2012; Brangwynne et al., 2015; Csizmok et al., 2016; Kato et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Linear multivalent proteins consist of multiple protein-protein/protein nucleic acid interaction domains or SLiMs connected by intrinsically disordered linkers that lack specific interaction motifs.
source: The simplest multivalent proteins are linear polymers that consist of multiple protein-protein/protein nucleic acid interaction domains or SLiMs connected by intrinsically disordered linkers that lack specific interaction motifs (Figure 1a).
evidence: This is a definitional statement illustrated by Figure 1a.

claim: Linear multivalent proteins may be classified as associative polymers.
source: Linear multivalent proteins may be classified as associative polymers (Tanaka, 2011; Semenov and Rubinstein, 1998), with specific intra- and intermolecular associations being mediated by non-covalent interactions amongst domains or motifs.
evidence: This classification is supported by citations to theoretical work on associative polymers.

claim: Physical gels are defined by specific, reversible non-covalent interactions that represent physical crosslinks between protein modules/SLiMs and their ligands.
source: Physical gels (referred to hereafter as gels) are defined by specific, reversible non-covalent interactions, that represent physical crosslinks between protein modules/SLiMs and their ligands (Su et al., 2016; Tanaka, 2011; Falkenberg et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a definitional statement supported by citations.

claim: The effective solvation volume (ves) of a linker can be pictured in terms of the impact that a linker has on bringing together interaction modules that are connected to either end.
source: The effective solvation volume (ves) of a linker can be pictured in terms of the impact that a linker has on bringing together interaction modules that are connected to either end (see Figure 2).
evidence: This is a conceptual explanation illustrated by Figure 2.

claim: When ves is positive, the linker is highly expanded and drives interaction modules apart.
source: When ves is positive, the linker is highly expanded and this outwards force repels the two interaction modules, driving them apart.
evidence: This is a theoretical explanation of the physical behavior of linkers with positive ves.

claim: When ves is negative, the linker is compact and pulls interaction modules close together.
source: When ves is negative, the linker is compact, and the hypothetical force pulls the two interaction modules inward, driving them close together.
evidence: This is a theoretical explanation of the physical behavior of linkers with negative ves.

claim: When ves is close to zero, the linker does not have strong interaction preferences and mimics a passive tether.
source: When ves is close to zero, the linker does not have strong interaction preferences and mimics a passive tether.
evidence: This is a theoretical explanation of the physical behavior of linkers with ves ≈ 0.

claim: The effective solvation volume of a linker is directly proportional to the second virial coefficient (B2).
source: The effective solvation volume is directly proportional to the second virial coefficient denoted as B2 (32, 41).
evidence: This is a theoretical relationship supported by citations.

claim: The effective solvation volume of a disordered linker is determined directly by its primary sequence.
source: Therefore, the effective solvation volume of a disordered linker is determined directly by its primary sequence.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the relationship between sequence composition and chain-chain/chain-solvent interactions.

claim: Approximately 100 linear multivalent proteins were identified from the non-redundant human proteome (20,162 sequences).
source: Using a stringent set of criteria (see Materials and methods section) we identified approximately 100 linear multivalent proteins from the non-redundant human proteome (20,162 sequences) and extracted 226 unique linker regions (see Materials and methods for details).
evidence: This is a result from the bioinformatics analysis performed in the study.

claim: 226 unique linker regions were extracted from linear multivalent proteins in the human proteome.
source: Using a stringent set of criteria (see Materials and methods section) we identified approximately 100 linear multivalent proteins from the non-redundant human proteome (20,162 sequences) and extracted 226 unique linker regions (see Materials and methods for details).
evidence: This is a result from the bioinformatics analysis performed in the study.

claim: Sequences deficient in charged residues are expected to have negative ves values.
source: Figure 3a shows that sequences deficient in charged residues are expected to have negative ves values, whereas sequences enriched in charges are expected to have positive ves values.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the all-atom simulation results shown in Figure 3a.

claim: Sequences enriched in charges are expected to have positive ves values.
source: Figure 3a shows that sequences deficient in charged residues are expected to have negative ves values, whereas sequences enriched in charges are expected to have positive ves values.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the all-atom simulation results shown in Figure 3a.

claim: Sequences that form compact globules have negative values of ves and negative values of ∆.
source: Sequences that form compact globules have negative values of ves and negative values of ∆.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the analysis of inter-residue distance profiles.

claim: For sequences with fractions of charged residues below 0.3, ves is negative.
source: For the sequences examined, this is true when the fractions of charged residues is below 0.3.
evidence: This is a result from the all-atom simulations of the fourteen sequences.

claim: Within an interval between 0.3 and 0.5 for the fraction of charged residues, sequences mimic the FRC limit where ves ≈ 0.
source: Within an interval between 0.3 and 0.5 for the fraction of charged residues, sequences mimic the FRC limit, where ves ≈ 0.
evidence: This is a result from the all-atom simulations of the fourteen sequences.

claim: Sequences with fractions of charged residues greater than 0.5 have positive ves values.
source: Sequences that prefer chain-solvent interactions to intra-chain interactions will be expanded relative to the FRC limit. This leads to positive values of ves and corresponds to values of ∆ that are greater than 0.1.
evidence: This is inferred from the discussion of sequences with ∆ > 0.1 and the relationship to charge content.

claim: Of the 226 unique linker sequences, approximately 30% have negative effective solvation volumes (∆ < –0.1).
source: Of the 226 unique linker sequences, approximately 30% have negative effective solvation volumes (∆ < –0.1) whereas 38% have sequences defined by ∆ values in the range –0.1 ≤ ∆≤0.1, implying that they will have near zero effective solvation volumes and are mimics of FRC linkers.
evidence: This is a result from the analysis of the distribution of ∆ values shown in Figure 3d.

claim: 38% of the 226 unique linker sequences have near zero effective solvation volumes (–0.1 ≤ ∆≤0.1).
source: Of the 226 unique linker sequences, approximately 30% have negative effective solvation volumes (∆ < –0.1) whereas 38% have sequences defined by ∆ values in the range –0.1 ≤ ∆≤0.1, implying that they will have near zero effective solvation volumes and are mimics of FRC linkers.
evidence: This is a result from the analysis of the distribution of ∆ values shown in Figure 3d.

claim: 30% of the 226 unique linker sequences have positive effective solvation volumes (∆ > 0.1).
source: Finally, 30% of linkers are characterized by ∆ values greater than 0.1, which means that their effective solvation volumes are positive.
evidence: This is a result from the analysis of the distribution of ∆ values shown in Figure 3d.

claim: 68% of naturally occurring disordered linkers have a positive or near positive effective solvation volume.
source: The key finding is that disordered linkers come in a range of sequence flavors, and 68% have a positive or near positive effective solvation volume.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the distribution analysis (38% + 30% = 68%).

claim: The proteins identified from the human proteome were significantly enriched for RNA/DNA binding and RNA localization.
source: The proteins we identified were significantly enriched for RNA/DNA binding and RNA localization, as assessed by PANTHER-GO enrichment analysis (Mi et al., 2017) (p<0.005).
evidence: This is a result from the Gene Ontology enrichment analysis.

claim: Linkers with negative effective solvation volumes serve as additional drivers of phase separation.
source: For linkers with negative effective solvation volumes the linkers serve as additional drivers of phase separation (Crick et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a conclusion supported by a citation and theoretical understanding.

claim: Each SH3 domain was assigned to a single lattice site in the coarse-grained model.
source: A single lattice site was assigned to each SH3 domain.
evidence: This is a description of the simulation model design.

claim: Each PRM was assigned to a single lattice site in the coarse-grained model.
source: Therefore, each PRM was also assigned to a single lattice site.
evidence: This is a description of the simulation model design.

claim: The spatial dimensions of a single SH3 domain corresponds to ~7 linker residues if ves ≥ 0.
source: Previous all-atom simulations showed that the spatial dimensions of a single SH3 domain corresponds to ~7 linker residues, if ves ≥ 0 (54).
evidence: This is a result from previous all-atom simulations cited in the manuscript.

claim: Individual SH3 domains and PRMs can bind to one another and form a 1:1 complex with an intrinsic binding energy of –2kBT.
source: Individual SH3 domains and PRMs can bind to one another and form a 1:1 complex with an intrinsic binding energy of –2kBT.
evidence: This is a parameter of the simulation model.

claim: The intrinsic affinity of –2kBT reproduces measured dissociation constants for SH3 domains and PRMs.
source: This intrinsic affinity reproduces measured dissociation constants for SH3 domains and PRMs (Li et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a validation of the model parameter against experimental data.

claim: For multivalent proteins with a valence of 5 or 7 and linker lengths in the range 3 ≤ n < 12 (or 21 ≤ N ≤ 84 residues), the value of c* is less than one.
source: For multivalent proteins with a valance of 5 or 7 and linker lengths in the range 3 ≤ n < 12 (or 21 ≤ N ≤ 84, where N is the number of linker residues), the value of c* is less than one, and the lowest values of c* are realized for linkers of length 3 < n < 6.
evidence: This is a result from the simulation analysis shown in Figure 8a.

claim: FRC linkers within a defined length range engender positive global cooperativity.
source: FRC linkers within a defined length range engender positive global cooperativity and for linker lengths in this optimal range, positive global cooperativity increases with increasing valence.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the simulation results shown in Figure 8a.

claim: For FRC linkers, positive global cooperativity increases with increasing valence.
source: FRC linkers within a defined length range engender positive global cooperativity and for linker lengths in this optimal range, positive global cooperativity increases with increasing valence.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the simulation results shown in Figure 8a.

claim: For long FRC linker lengths, c* converges to one implying that the domains interact independently.
source: Accordingly, for long linker lengths, c* converges to one implying that the domains interact independently when the FRC linkers are sufficiently long.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the simulation results shown in Figure 8a.

claim: For SARC linkers, c* is greater than one for all linker lengths.
source: Figure 8b shows a plot of c* as a function of linker lengths for 3:3, 5:5, and 7:7 systems with SARC linkers. Here, c* is greater than one for all the linker lengths.
evidence: This is a result from the simulation analysis shown in Figure 8b.

claim: SARC linkers suppress phase separation and shift the gel point to higher concentrations compared to the Flory-Stockmayer threshold.
source: Linkers with positive effective solvation volumes suppress phase separation and shift the gel point to higher concentrations when compared to the threshold predicted by Flory-Stockmayer theories.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the simulation results shown in Figure 8b.

claim: Approximately 30% of all linkers in the inventory will have 50 or fewer residues and ∆ values less than 0.1.
source: Our analysis of linker sequences in linear multivalent systems shows that approximately 30% of all linkers in the inventory will have 50 or fewer residues and ∆ values less than 0.1 (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a result from the proteome-wide analysis.

claim: Linkers with 50 or fewer residues and ∆ values less than 0.1 are the most likely candidates for enabling gelation driven by phase separation in linear multivalent proteins.
source: These linkers are the most likely candidates for enabling gelation driven by phase separation in linear multivalent proteins.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined proteome analysis and simulation results.

claim: Approximately 18% of all linkers have fewer than 50 residues and ∆ values greater than 0.1.
source: Approximately, 18% of all linkers have fewer than 50 residues and ∆ values greater than 0.1.
evidence: This is a result from the proteome-wide analysis.

claim: Linkers with fewer than 50 residues and ∆ values greater than 0.1 are the most likely candidates for weakening phase separation.
source: These are the most likely candidates for weakening phase separation and sequences with large positive values of ∆ will drive gelation without phase separation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined proteome analysis and simulation results.

claim: Approximately 50% of linkers are longer than 50 residues and are unlikely to be major modulators of gelation transitions.
source: The remainder of the linkers,~50% in all, are longer than 50 residues and these are unlikely to be major modulators of gelation transitions since the analysis in Figure 8 suggests that these linkers cross into the Flory-Stockmayer limit, where the interaction modules become independent of one another.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined proteome analysis and simulation results.

claim: For affinities below 3kBT, the 5:5 system with hybrid five-site linkers undergoes a continuous transition from a sol to a gel.
source: For affinities below 3kBT, the system undergoes a continuous transition from a sol to a gel and the green dashed line demarcates the sol-gel line.
evidence: This is a result from the phase diagram shown in Figure 9.

claim: The critical point for the 5:5 system with hybrid five-site linkers is defined by a critical interaction affinity of 3kBT and a critical module concentration of ~10–3 polymers/voxel.
source: The critical point for this system, shown as a red asterisk, is defined jointly by a critical interaction affinity (3kBT) and a critical module concentration (~10–3polymers/voxel).
evidence: This is a result from the phase diagram shown in Figure 9.

claim: The width of the two-phase regime increases with interaction affinity.
source: The width of the two-phase regime increases with interaction affinity.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the phase diagrams shown in Figures 9 and 10.

claim: Phase separation is realized at lower concentrations of the interacting domains as interaction affinity increases.
source: This implies that phase separation is realized at lower concentrations of the interacting domains and is depicted by a leftward shift of the arm shown in light blue in Figure 9.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the phase diagram shown in Figure 9.

claim: The critical point shifts to higher interaction affinities as the effective solvation volumes of linkers increase.
source: Progressing from the top left corner to the bottom right corner, we find that the critical point shifts to higher interaction affinities as the effective solvation volumes of linkers increase.
evidence: This is a result from the phase diagrams shown in Figure 10.

claim: For a given value of the affinity, the width of the two-phase regime increases as the magnitude of the effective solvation volume decreases.
source: For a given value of the affinity, the width of the two-phase regime increases as the magnitude of the effective solvation volume decreases.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the phase diagrams shown in Figure 10.

claim: For high effective solvation volumes of linkers, the presence of a two-phase regime is discernible only for very high affinities.
source: In fact, for high effective solvation volumes of linkers, the presence of a two-phase regime is discernible only for very high affinities and phase transitions occur mainly via gelation without phase separation.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the phase diagrams shown in Figure 10.

claim: The numerical results are consistent with the theoretical predictions of Semenov and Rubinstein.
source: Our numerical results summarized in Figures 6–10 are consistent with the theoretical predictions of Semenov and Rubinstein.
evidence: This is a comparison of the simulation results to prior theoretical work.

claim: There is an optimal range of linker lengths that supports gelation driven by phase separation for a given interaction affinity between domains.
source: We have also shown that the effective solvation volumes of linkers are directly determined by their primary sequences (Figure 3). Finally, there appears to be an optimal range of linker lengths that supports gelation driven by phase separation for a given interaction affinity between domains.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the simulation results shown in Figure 8.

claim: Linkers with negative ves values can engage in non-specific attractive interactions with interaction domains as well as other linkers.
source: They can also engage in non-specific attractive interactions with interaction domains as well as other linkers of different sequence composition that have negative ves values.
evidence: This is a theoretical explanation of the behavior of linkers with negative ves.

claim: Linkers with negative ves values lead to an effective shortening of the linker length due to linker compaction.
source: Linkers with negative ves values have two distinct effects: firstly, they lead to be an effective shortening of the linker length due to linker compaction, and secondly they can engage in additional in trans interactions causing an increase in the effective valence.
evidence: This is a theoretical explanation of the behavior of linkers with negative ves.

claim: Linkers with negative ves values are likely to yield significantly more dense droplets when compared to linkers with near zero or positive ves values.
source: Linkers with negative ves values are likely to yield significantly more dense droplets when compared to linkers with near zero or positive ves values.
evidence: This is a conclusion supported by comparison to experimental measurements.

claim: The intra-droplet concentration for the RGG domain of LAF-1, which has a positive ves value, is two orders of magnitude smaller than the intra-droplet concentration measured for elastin-like polypeptides, which have negative ves values.
source: The intra-droplet concentration for the RGG domain of LAF-1 (41), which has a positive ves value, is two orders of magnitude smaller than the intra-droplet concentration measured for elastin-like polypeptides (Simon et al., 2017), which have negative ves values.
evidence: This is a comparison of experimental measurements from cited studies.

claim: The regulation of cell signaling by phase transitions might predominantly involve gelation driven by phase separation.
source: We speculate that the regulation of cell signaling by phase transitions might predominantly involve gelation driven by phase separation.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the study's findings and biological observations.

claim: The formation of dense droplets will increase local protein concentrations, facilitating a cooperative amplification in signal transduction.
source: The role of phase separation in cell signaling likely reflects the fact that the formation of dense droplets will increase local protein concentrations, facilitating a cooperative amplification in signal transduction as distinct signaling components undergo efficient intermolecular phosphorylation due to the high local concentration (Su et al., 2016; Hernández-Vega et al., 2017; Woodruff et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a mechanistic explanation supported by citations.

claim: Gelation within a droplet will contribute directly to the droplet sub-structure and to the spatial organization of components within droplets.
source: Gelation within a droplet will contribute directly to the droplet sub-structure and to the spatial organization of components within droplets (Li et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a conclusion supported by a citation.

claim: The extent and dynamics of crosslinking within a droplet-spanning gel will directly influence the material properties of droplets.
source: The extent and dynamics of crosslinking within a droplet-spanning gel will directly influence the material properties of droplets (Tanaka, 2011).
evidence: This is a conclusion supported by a citation to theoretical work.

claim: The measured features of the squid lens are readily explained using the framework of patchy colloid theory.
source: However, the measured features of the squid lens are readily explained using the framework of patchy colloid theory (Bianchi et al., 2006; Bianchi et al., 2008), whereby the polydispersity of disordered loops in S-crystallin determine the extent of physical crosslinking giving rise to gels of different densities across the lens (Cai et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a conclusion from a cited study on S-crystallin proteins.

claim: Effective scaffolding proteins for gelation driven by phase separation are likely to be linear multivalent proteins with linkers that have low effective solvation volumes (ves ≈ 0).
source: We further propose that effective scaffolding proteins for gelation driven by phase separation are likely to be linear multivalent proteins with linkers that have low effective solvation volumes (ves ≈ 0).
evidence: This is a proposal based on the study's findings.

claim: Proteins with linkers that have large positive ves values are likely to be clients that partition into the droplets formed by the scaffolds.
source: Proteins with linkers that have large positive ves values are likely to be clients that partition into the droplets formed by the scaffolds (Banani et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a proposal based on the study's findings and supported by a citation.

claim: The effective solvation volumes of linkers in linear multivalent protein can be tuned through synergistic actions of kinases and phosphatases.
source: For example, the effective solvation volumes of linkers in linear multivalent protein can be tuned through synergistic actions of kinases and phosphatases (Bergeron-Sandoval et al., 2016; Kwon et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a proposal supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The substrates for multisite phosphorylation tend to be enriched in disordered regions with positive effective solvation volumes.
source: Support for this proposal comes from the observation that the substrates for multisite phosphorylation tend to be enriched in disordered regions with positive effective solvation volumes (Holehouse et al., 2017; Martin et al., 2016).
evidence: This is an observation supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Posttranscriptional processing of mRNA transcripts via alternative splicing can be a route for making tissue-specific alterations to linker sequences.
source: Additionally, posttranscriptional processing of mRNA transcripts via alternative splicing can also be a route for making tissue-specific alterations to linker sequences.
evidence: This is a proposal based on biological mechanisms.

claim: Transcripts coding for disordered regions are preferentially targeted by tissue-specific splice factors when compared to transcripts for folded domains.
source: Interestingly, transcripts coding for disordered regions are preferentially targeted by tissue-specific splice factors when compared to transcripts for folded domains (Buljan et al., 2013; Buljan et al., 2012).
evidence: This is an observation supported by citations to prior work.
